query: All five members of the Maple Street group shared their views on the proposed residents' parking scheme. What was each person's position and reasoning?
gold: All five weighed in with distinct positions and reasons: Claudette was against — she objected on cost grounds ('£80 a year is an additional burden on residents who have always parked freely here') and felt paying for previously free parking was wrong. Marcus was in favour — his reason was child safety at the school gate, where pavement parking creates danger during the school run. Jordan was neutral — they have no car and the scheme does not affect them directly, though they noted empathy for those on tight budgets. Femi was broadly in favour but had one reservation: displaced commuter parking moving to neighbouring streets. Vera was in favour — her reason was professional: home visits mean she needs parking near the house on clinic days.
context:
[1] (about=Claudette, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T15:28:00) I have mixed feelings. I understand the frustration with commuter parking. But £80 a year is an additional burden on residents who have always parked freely here. I remember when you could park outside your own home without paying for the privilege. I am not convinced.
[2] (about=Vera, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:03:00) Support the scheme. Home visits mean I need parking here on clinic days.
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T15:35:00) I'm in favour. As a parent, the school gate situation is untenable, people park on the pavement all morning. Permits would fix that overnight.
[4] (about=Claudette, episodic, t6 @2025-05-26T21:18:00) residents only feels right to me. It keeps the day neighbourly
[5] (about=Femi, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:15:00) Good to have views from everyone. So: Vera and Marcus in favour, Claudette against, Jordan neutral, me broadly yes with caveats. I'll represent that range at the consultation meeting. Thanks all.
[6] (about=Jordan, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:17:00) if they do it I'd want a review after a year tbh
[7] (about=Vera, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:19:00) a review clause would be sensible
[8] (about=Claudette, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T18:21:00) a trial period I could live with. Permanence is what irritates me
[9] (about=Femi, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T15:49:00) I'm broadly in favour. My concern is the commuter overflow onto the next street.
[10] (about=Claudette, episodic, t8 @2025-06-02T16:19:00) Femi, you have done Len proud. I was quite emotional seeing the whole street out together. This is what Maple Street is for, people, not parking schemes.
agent_answer:
Based on the conversation:

- **Claudette** – **Against** the scheme as proposed (Femi describes her as "against"). She has mixed feelings: she understands the frustration with commuter parking, but objects to the £80-a-year charge as an added burden on residents who have always parked free. She says permanence is what irritates her; she "could live with" a trial period. (She later says "residents only feels right" to her for keeping the street neighbourly.)

- **Vera** – **In favour.** She supports the scheme because her home visits mean she needs parking on the street on clinic days. She also agrees that a review clause would be sensible.

- **Marcus** – **In favour.** As a parent, he finds the school-gate situation untenable, with people parking on the pavement all morning; he believes permits would fix that.

- **Jordan** – **Neutral / conditional.** If the scheme goes ahead, Jordan would want a review after a year ("if they do it I'd want a review after a year tbh"). Femi summarizes Jordan's position as neutral.

- **Femi** – **Broadly in favour, with caveats.** His stated concern is the commuter overflow being pushed onto the next street. He describes himself as "broadly yes with caveats" and plans to represent the range of views at the consultation meeting.
